question: Does supervising every next token create an optimization bias that improves out-of-distribution reasoning relative to training only on answer-critical tokens?

key_findings.claim: The paper contrasts next-token prediction with critical-token prediction while holding architecture and reasoning examples broadly fixed.
key_findings.evidence: NTP incurs loss on intermediate and filler tokens as well as answers; CTP masks the objective to selected output-critical positions. Synthetic anchor functions, PrOntoQA variants, PARARULE, SimpleLogic, and classification controls provide several reasoning regimes.

key_findings.claim: CTP often learns the target faster in distribution, but NTP generalizes more robustly on reversal, composition, perturbation, and subsequent-task tests.
key_findings.evidence: Training and accuracy curves show early CTP gains followed by memorization or overfitting on several splits, whereas NTP reaches flatter solutions and higher held-out reasoning accuracy. NTP-pretrained models also improve later CTP fine-tuning relative to CTP-only histories.

key_findings.claim: The proposed mechanism is regularization by gradients from nominally noncritical tokens, with a two-stage trajectory from distribution flattening to fitting the reasoning relation.
key_findings.evidence: Gradient and representation analyses report that the auxiliary-token contribution decreases during training while initially discouraging sharp shortcut solutions. Perturbation tests and loss-landscape plots associate NTP with greater parameter/input robustness and flatter minima.

key_findings.claim: The experiments establish a bias in small controlled settings, not that ordinary web-scale NTP is sufficient or universally superior for reasoning.
key_findings.evidence: Most causal comparisons use compact transformers and synthetic/formal datasets where the authors can choose critical positions. Natural language scale, tokenizer effects, data quality, and post-training objectives are not jointly varied, and flatness is correlated with rather than proven to cause generalization.

method.core_idea: Use loss masking as a controlled intervention to isolate what the dense sequence supervision of NTP contributes beyond direct answer supervision.
method.mechanism: Models are trained either on all next tokens or only designated critical tokens, then compared on learning speed, OOD accuracy, transfer, parameter/input perturbation, flatness, and gradient evolution. Noise controls test whether structured auxiliary-token gradients behave like generic injected noise.
assumptions: The selected critical tokens contain the task's direct reasoning target and the mask does not remove necessary supervision asymmetrically.
Synthetic filler and intermediate tokens reproduce the optimization role of natural language context.
Reported flatness measures are comparable across solutions and parameter scales.
Small-model controlled findings extrapolate at least qualitatively to pretrained language models.

techniques.role: Constructs a direct objective-level control for dense NTP supervision.
Tests whether learned relations transfer beyond memorized direction or templates.
Tracks the contribution of noncritical-token losses over training.
Relates objective choice to robustness around the learned solution.

evaluations.setting: Original and cloze PrOntoQA plus reversed-rule evaluation.
evaluations.metric: Training and held-out reasoning accuracy over epochs.
evaluations.result: CTP fits quickly but overfits or degrades on the reversal split; NTP learns more slowly and reaches stronger stable generalization.
evaluations.baseline: Critical-token prediction with the same model and data.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic anchor-function compositions padded with controlled token sequences.
evaluations.metric: Accuracy on unseen compositions and reverse mappings.
evaluations.result: Dense next-token supervision improves extrapolation, while generic noise injection does not consistently reproduce the effect.

evaluations.setting: Multi-task fine-tuning and parameter/input perturbations across reasoning datasets.
evaluations.metric: Downstream task accuracy, sensitivity to perturbation, and local loss increase.
evaluations.result: NTP-pretrained checkpoints adapt better with later CTP and occupy flatter, more robust regions under the reported probes.
evaluations.baseline: CTP-pretrained then CTP-fine-tuned models and random-noise controls.

limitations: Most experiments use small transformers and synthetic or templated reasoning corpora.
Critical-token labels are task-dependent and may create a disadvantaged objective by removing useful intermediate supervision.
Flatness metrics are sensitive to parameterization and do not prove a causal mechanism.
The study does not compare NTP with contemporary multi-token, denoising, process-supervision, or reinforcement-learning objectives at matched scale.
failure_modes: Auxiliary tokens can encode shortcuts or noise that hurts rather than regularizes.
A critical-token mask can accidentally omit intermediate variables required for learnability.
NTP's greater sample/step cost may outweigh its generalization benefit on easy downstream tasks.
Local flatness can be changed by reparameterization without changing model behavior.
reusable_insights: Loss masking is a clean way to test what dense generative supervision adds to an answer-only objective.
Optimization speed and rule generalization should be reported separately; the faster-fitting objective can generalize worse.
Structured auxiliary targets may regularize differently from isotropic gradient noise.
open_questions: Which classes of auxiliary tokens help, and can they be selected adaptively rather than all-or-nothing?
Does the NTP advantage persist at fixed compute and data scale in modern pretrained models?
How does dense token supervision interact with multi-token prediction, process rewards, and RL post-training?

competitive_landscape.title: The Pitfalls of Next-Token Prediction
competitive_landscape.relationship: Analyzes structural tasks for which next-token prediction can learn undesirable solutions or fail to represent global properties.
competitive_landscape.difference: It emphasizes limitations of the NTP objective; this paper isolates a beneficial regularization bias relative to answer-token-only training on selected reasoning tasks.

competitive_landscape.title: Better & Faster Large Language Models via Multi-token Prediction
competitive_landscape.relationship: Changes the training target from one future token to several and reports improved representation learning and sample efficiency.
competitive_landscape.difference: Multi-token prediction adds future targets to NTP; this paper removes noncritical targets to measure the regularizing role of dense sequential supervision.

competitive_landscape.title: How Reinforcement Learning After Next-Token Prediction Facilitates Learning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Studies how reinforcement learning changes learning after an NTP-pretrained initialization.
competitive_landscape.difference: It examines a post-training objective transition; the present work compares NTP with critical-token supervision during supervised training and attributes differences to optimization bias.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Dense NTP gradients introduce a reasoning-favorable bias that yields flatter minima, robustness, and better downstream rule learning than critical-token prediction.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Matched loss-mask comparisons, transfer tests, perturbations, and gradient trajectories repeatedly distinguish slower fitting from stronger generalization.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The masking intervention is informative and the speed/generalization reversal is robust within the suite, but the proposed mechanism and scaling beyond synthetic tasks remain hypotheses.
